Plant diversity:
Plants are living things that make their own food by photosynthesis. Their cells have cell walls, and they contain chlorophyll in chloroplasts. Plants are placed in two main groups: nonvascular plants and vascular plants.

Nonvascular plants, such as mosses, have no true roots, stems or leaves and no tubes for carrying water. They are small and live in damp places. Vascular plants have xylem tubes that carry water and phloem tubes that carry food. They include ferns, which reproduce by spores, gymnosperms, which make seeds in cones, and angiosperms, which make seeds inside flowers and fruits. Angiosperms are the largest group and are split into monocots and dicots.
Roots, stems and leaves:
Roots hold the plant in the soil and absorb water and minerals. Root hairs greatly increase the absorbing surface. Taproots are thick and deep. Fibrous roots are thin and spread widely.

Stems support the plant and carry materials. Xylem carries water and minerals upward from the roots. Phloem carries sugar made in the leaves to all parts. Stems can also store food.

Leaves are the main place of photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen, using light energy. Gases move through small pores called stomata. Guard cells open and close the stomata. Water vapor leaving through the stomata is called transpiration.
Flowers, seeds and fruits:
A flower is the reproductive organ of an angiosperm. Its main parts are sepals, petals, stamens and the pistil. The stamen is the male part: it has an anther that makes pollen, held on a filament. The pistil is the female part: it has a stigma, a style and an ovary that contains ovules.

After fertilization, each ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit. A seed contains an embryo, stored food and a seed coat. Monocot seeds have one seed leaf (cotyledon). Dicot seeds have two. Fruits protect seeds and help to spread them.
Reproduction in plants:
Plants reproduce in two ways. Sexual reproduction needs two sex cells that join in fertilization, and the offspring differ from the parents. Asexual reproduction needs only one parent, and the offspring are identical copies of it.

In flowering plants, pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma. Wind, insects, birds and water can carry pollen. Pollen then grows a tube to the ovule, and fertilization makes a seed. Seeds are spread by wind, water, animals or explosion. A seed germinates when it has water, oxygen and a suitable temperature.

Vegetative propagation uses roots, stems or leaves, for example runners, tubers, bulbs and cuttings.
